I've noticed that the `Mobile` render is much better than `Compatibility` for newer devices.

It should be possible to publish different versions for different API levels or devices with higher Vulkan support.
https://developer.android.com/google/play/publishing/multiple-apks 
https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-feature-element#vulkan-hw-features

However, the export feature can only include different architectures in the AAB. I wonder if this can be done manually.
- This can help too https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6423

-It will be definitely Cool to have a way to publish an app in both Vulkan and OpenGL versions!

And even better if we could point the users to each version separatedly;
this may even be necessary in some cases for Compat or Performance reasons..

So it could eventually ease technical support by not having to address each case individually..

> -It will be definitely Cool to have a way to publish an app in both Vulkan and OpenGL versions!

I may be wrong, but I think it should already be possible! See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97142

The first 3 provided errors relate to libGLESv2_powervr.so - this is the OpenGL ES driver for PowerVR GPUs - which i think was also highlighted in #101529

the last crash seems unrelated to this - that one could be to do with the google ads plugin

could a solution in this case be to identify which effects / textures are causing this and disable them based of `OS.get_video_adapter_driver_info()`? essentially have a slightly reduced experience for for users of older devices.

> So yes, as I wrote on the forum, we tested the ANGLE fallback and have a more advanced implementation that can detect problematic drivers at runtime and fall back to ANGLE when required.

Driver-related crashes like this are very difficult to fix without being able to reproduce them on a device with the same chipset and driver version. This would not be reproducible in an emulator, as it does not use the same driver. The most effective next step would be to obtain such a device and try to trigger the crash, ideally by testing the most resource-intensive in-game scenarios first. Once the issue can be reliably reproduced, it becomes much easier to investigate and apply a fix.
